_comment: The backend's defaults, in one place.
These are not the card's own choices. normalize_config() in the mmwave-fusion
integration fills in exactly these values for anything a configuration leaves
out, and the editor has to show the same numbers or it reports settings the
system is not using. It did: track_ttl_s was written as 1.8 in two places in
editor.ts while the backend used 1.2, so the field showed a value no fused
Kept as JSON rather than as TypeScript constants so the other side can read it
too: tests/unit/test_fusion_defaults_match.py in the workspace repo loads this
file and asserts it equals what normalize_config() produces, key for key. A
setting added to the backend without being reflected here fails that test,
which is the only thing that makes this file stay true.

conditional._comment: A vital-signs radar reports slowly enough that the normal track timeout drops people who are only breathing, so the backend raises it whenever one is present.
